text:
Evidence supports simple behavioral baselines more strongly than probe-driven model selection. A [15-dataset shuffling study](https://publications.hse.ru/en/chapters/984043670) found weak sequential structure in several popular benchmarks. [Petrov et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19833) showed recency-weighted pairwise models outperforming reproduced eSASRec by 15–38% on three Amazon datasets, while losing substantially on MovieLens-20M. These are predictive baselines, not evidence that perturbation sensitivity forecasts which intervention will improve ranking. No directly matching prospective calibration evidence emerged from this search, especially for the four specified Amazon categories.

Sensitivity measures dependence on history; it does not establish whether that dependence helps prediction. Shuffling changes recency as well as order, so useful controls include shuffling only the older prefix while preserving the last item, truncating older history, last-item-only prediction, and recency-weighted pooling. Separately, [recency-sampling experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) demonstrated accuracy and training-efficiency benefits across sequential architectures, including SASRec. This motivates testing recency interventions, but does not validate sensitivity as their selection criterion.

Recommendation: prioritize one bounded predictive experiment over another broad calibration expansion. Before observing new validation results, freeze the probe definition, predicted intervention benefit, baseline/intervention configurations, checkpoint rule, minimum useful macro-HR@10 gain, and GPU budget. Preserve all four categories, prescribed seeds, splits, and evaluator; compare paired user outcomes and report category effects alongside the macro result. Allow no validation-driven variants after this comparison. [Adaptive holdout research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) explains why repeated feedback can overfit validation. A fixed comparison limits additional adaptation; it cannot erase prior reuse or establish general probe calibration. Reserve that claim for independent prospective evidence.
